problem_summary.summary: Merge k ascending singly linked lists into one ascending linked list.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: ListNode[] lists whose non-null heads begin sorted linked lists. Return the merged head; ListNode is provided by the judge.
constraints: The total number of nodes is at most 10^4

brute_force.explanation: Collect every value from every input list, sort all values, and build a fresh output list. This simple baseline is useful when node reuse is undesirable, but it ignores the input lists' existing order.
brute_force.correctness_idea: The collected values contain exactly the union of all list elements, including duplicates. Sorting puts them in ascending order, and building one node per value preserves that complete multiset.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(k + N log N), where k is the number of list heads and N is the total number of nodes; scanning empty heads costs O(k).
brute_force.space_complexity: O(N) auxiliary values plus O(N) newly allocated output nodes.

optimized.explanation: Recursively divide the array of list heads into halves, merge each half, and combine the two sorted results with a standard two-list pointer merge. Existing nodes are reused.
optimized.correctness_idea: The base case is one already sorted list. Each recursive result contains all nodes from its input subrange in sorted order; merging two sorted results preserves order and retains every node. Induction over the range splits proves the final result is sorted and complete.
optimized.time_complexity: O(1) for k <= 1; for k >= 2, O(k + N log k), where k is the number of list heads and N is the total number of nodes. Each recursion-tree level merges each node at most once.
optimized.space_complexity: O(log k) recursion stack for k > 0, plus O(1) merge pointers; the input list nodes are reused.

steps.condition: The range has more than one head.
Compare current heads and select the smaller each time.
steps.action: Link 1, then 2, then 4, then append the remaining 5.

steps.condition: The first half is [1,2,4,5] and the second is [3,6].

edge_cases.handling: The range is empty and null is returned.
Recursive base results and two-list merges remain null, so the final result is null.
It is returned unchanged by the single-list base case.
The <= branch chooses from the first run; all duplicate nodes are still linked into the result.
